table_assessment.assessment_notes: Exact review confirms exercise, dietary, weight-management, referral, monitoring, and assessment instructions. The same continuation cell also contains expected-outcome statements and an underspecified medication-therapy modification, so it is mixed content and not structurally ready without human adjudication.

entities.surface_form: most days (at least 3 days/week and preferably 6–7 days/week)

normative_assertions.notes: The table's component format supplies the recommendation semantics for aerobic-training frequency.
The table's component format supplies the recommendation semantics for resistance/strength-training frequency.

text_units.verbatim_text: • Frequency: most days (at least 3 days/week and preferably 6–7 days/week) for aerobic training; 2 times/week for resistance/strength training

normative_assertions.notes: The table specifies the intensity component for endurance continuous training.
Higher-intensity bouts are conditioned on the selected protocol.
The speech rule is an optional intensity-control tool when HR cannot be used.
The source specifies repetition and 1-RM ranges for resistance/strength training.

text_units.verbatim_text: • Intensity: moderate (i.e. 45–59% of peak oxygen consumption, 50–70% of W_{peak} (above the first ventilatory threshold), 55–69% of peak heart rate, 40–59% of heart rate reserve (to be calculated on top of rest HR), 4–6 METs, or 12/20–14/20 of the Borg scale) or moderate-to-high intensity for endurance continuous training. Higher intensities of exercise bouts for endurance high intensity interval training according to the selected protocol. The ‘speech rule’ (i.e. the respiratory rate should allow conversation) could be considered as an additional tool to control intensity when HR cannot be used. 30–70% of the 1-RM for the upper body and 40–80% of 1-RM for lower body exercises, with 12–15 repetitions in one set for resistance/strength training

entities.surface_form: at least 20–30 min (preferably 45–60 min) per session

normative_assertions.notes: Duration applies to the exercise-training component inherited from the table context.

text_units.verbatim_text: • Time: at least 20–30 min (preferably 45–60 min) per session

normative_assertions.notes: These are source-listed exercise-training types.
Coordination and other non-conventional training types are optional.

text_units.verbatim_text: • Type: aerobic training (walking, jogging, cycling, swimming, rowing, stair climbing, elliptical trainers, and aerobic dancing), resistance/strength training, flexibility training, balance training, and inspiratory muscle training. Coordination training and other types (non-conventional) may be considered

normative_assertions.notes: The imperative directs arrangement of exercise training to the stated weekly energy consumption.

text_units.verbatim_text: • Arrange exercise training in order to provide an energy consumption of 1000–2000 kcal/week

entities.surface_form: before, during and after exercise training
patients with new symptoms, signs, BP abnormalities and increased supraventricular or ventricular ectopy during exercise
to verify individual responses and tolerability, clinical stability, and promptly identify signs and symptoms indicating to modify or terminate the programme

normative_assertions.notes: A supervised in-hospital programme is optional during initial phases based on individual features.
The source explicitly specifies supervision content and timing.
Prolonged supervision is conditional on the listed new symptoms, signs, BP abnormalities, or ectopy.

text_units.verbatim_text: • During the initial phases (duration based on individual features) supervised, in-hospital exercise training programme may be recommended, especially, to verify individual responses and tolerability, clinical stability, and promptly identify signs and symptoms indicating to modify or terminate the programme. The supervision should include physical examination, monitoring of HR, BP and rhythm before, during and after exercise training. The supervised period should be prolonged in patients with new symptoms, signs, BP abnormalities and increased supraventricular or ventricular ectopy during exercise

entities.surface_form: Weight reduction by means of diet, exercise and behaviour modification
BMI \geq 30 \text{ kg/m}^2 , or waist circumference \geq 102 \text{ cm} in men or \geq 88 \text{ cm} in women
BMI \geq 25 \text{ kg/m}^2 , or waist circumference \geq 94 \text{ cm} in men or \geq 80 \text{ cm} in women
multiple risk factors (such as hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, smoking and insulin resistance or diabetes)

normative_assertions.notes: Weight reduction is recommended for the source-defined obese group.
Weight reduction should be considered for overweight patients, particularly with multiple risk factors.

text_units.verbatim_text: • Weight reduction by means of diet, exercise and behaviour modification. It is recommended in obese patients ( BMI \geq 30 \text{ kg/m}^2 , or waist circumference \geq 102 \text{ cm} in men or \geq 88 \text{ cm} in women), and should be considered in overweight patients ( BMI \geq 25 \text{ kg/m}^2 , or waist circumference \geq 94 \text{ cm} in men or \geq 80 \text{ cm} in women), particularly if associated with multiple risk factors (such as hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, smoking and insulin resistance or diabetes)
